title: RAW: independently annotated manner classes predict held-phone contexts beyond binary C/V
summary: Use official CMU phone-type metadata to test transfer among stop/fricative/nasal/liquid/etc categories, withholding each predecessor phone identity from its training context table. Unlike1279 exact-ID advantage, this asks whether an independently supplied articulatory taxonomy predicts contexts of another phone. Procedural controls retain scope limits.

contract.source: Reuse unchanged1347 CMU TRAIN/TEST phone records and official phones metadata. Reuse both procedural packets; no new dictionary or native data.
contract.prediction: For each of24nonvowel phones p, exclude all training transitions whose predecessor is p. Fit next-phone distributions pooled by the independently specified manner of the predecessor, and compare with pooling all nonvowels. Score fixed TEST transitions after p at strictly inner positions. No exact-p parameter can predict p because it was withheld from training contexts.
contract.estimator_obligation: Root must freeze smoothing, context conditioning, event weights and gate before scoring; no automatic order/position extension. Keep same target support for both models. This is a RAW contract, not a completed preregistration.
contract.singletons: The aspirate category contains only HH. Leave-one-phone-out has no same-manner exemplar there, so use explicit baseline fallback and report zero-information capacity; do not omit this category after scoring.
contract.discriminatory_control: Compare official category table with fixed size-preserving random permutations of manner labels inside the24nonvowels, with number/seeds frozen before scoring. Apply same size vector to the24address-role symbols in each procedural source. Its fifteen values supply the other coarse class. These artificial sublabels have no articulatory interpretation.
contract.claim: A positive official-taxonomy advantage on CMU but not procedural sources would show transfer associated with independently supplied articulatory labels in this control. It is not unsupervised recovery of named sounds, morphology or a general origin classifier. It differs from merely finding that exact identity improves over binary labels.
limits: Only one modern dictionary; manner categories need not form perfectly homogeneous contextual classes.
A nonphonetic renderer with structured subroles can mimic this result; current procedural negatives do not cover every such system.
Native use would need an independently justified unit and category binding, not label-fitting until success.
A failed estimator does not disprove phonetic categories or higher-order phonology.
